label: Netonix WS-12-400-AC WISP Switch
description: Managed passive-PoE WISP switch: 12x 1G RJ45 PoE sources plus 2x 1G SFP uplinks, 110/220 VAC input with a 400 W supply, enough to power 24 GHz airFIBER and Mimosa radios from the tower.

poe.note: 400 W is the power supply rating the vendor quotes; the spec sheet prints 'N/A' for maximum power consumption, so there is no published box-plus-PoE ceiling to subtract from. 400 W is the only figure either source gives and is used as the PoE ceiling.

fabric.note: Netonix publishes 'Total Non-Blocking Line Rate' as the sum of one-directional port bandwidth (12x1G + 2x1G = 14 Gbps; 24x1G + 2x1G = 26 Gbps), not the duplex-doubled figure other vendors print as 'switching capacity'. Like for like with a FortiSwitch's 128 Gbps for 24x1G + 4x10G, these are half the number: 28 Gbps and 52 Gbps duplex.

notes: Store page: '110 / 220 VAC 400 Watt Power Supply, (12) Gbps POE Ports, (2) SFP Uplink Ports', explicitly marketed as powering airFIBER / Mimosa / SAF radios. Spec sheet: 330 x 228 x 44 mm, 3 kg, forced-air cooling, Vitesse core, MIPS 24K 416 MHz, 128 MB RAM, 16 MB flash, -25 to 55 C, CE/FCC/IC, 24 kV ESD. 24VH on ports 1-2 and 48VH on ports 1-6. Same 44 mm height as the 250 W model but 107 mm deeper and 1 kg heavier - the bigger supply is the difference, and it is the reason the 400 W unit is a 330 mm box. Passive PoE, software-configurable per port in the UI/CLI, not 802.3af/at: 24V and 48V at 1 A on pins 4,5(+)/7,8(-), 24VH and 48VH at 2 A on pins 1,2,4,5(+)/3,6,7,8(-) pairs. Current sensor per port. A port's wattage is therefore set by the voltage and current limit a human picks, which is why the port carries no wattage class here - only the unit's published ceiling does. Software from the same spec sheet: LACP/static LAG, STP/RSTP/MSTP/ERPS, port mirroring, VLAN dot1Q/QinQ/port trunking, SNMP, SMTP alerts, per-port bandwidth limiting, QoS, per-port ping watchdog, scheduled port bouncing, cable diagnostics, loop protection, DHCP snooping, IGMP snooping, flow control, storm control, multicast filtering, port isolation, auto TFTP backup on config change, UDP (Ubiquiti discovery), CDP and LLDP, ACLs plus login tarpit. Nothing in the sheet routes IP between VLANs, so this is l2-forward only. Management is HTTPS on 192.168.1.20 (admin/admin) with the host on 192.168.1.0/24, and a RS-232 serial console at 115200 8-N-1, no parity, XON/XOFF flow control, null-modem cable.
